memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'...I will remember my covenant with Jacob and my covenant with Isaac
and my covenant with Abraham, and I will remember the land'"
- Lev 26:42b (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Three names anchor the hope of return: Jacob, Isaac, Abraham. God says He
will remember His covenant with each of them. The people's hope of restoration
did not rest on their own faithfulness — which had failed completely — but
on the promises God had made generations before.

This is the bedrock of biblical hope. When everything on our side has
collapsed, God's covenant still stands. He remembers His promises even when
we forget ours.

Notice too that God reaches back to Abraham. The covenant with Abraham was
one of grace — God binding Himself by promise before Abraham had done
anything to deserve it. When later generations failed under the law, God's
answer was to reach back to that older promise of grace.

Dear reader, Paul makes exactly this argument. He says the promise to
Abraham came by faith, before the law, so that it might rest on grace and
be guaranteed to all Abraham's offspring (Rom 4:16). And he declares that
if we belong to Christ, then we are Abraham's seed, heirs according to the
promise (Gal 3:29).

Do you see the wonder? The covenant God remembered for exiled Israel is
the same line of promise that reaches us in Christ. Our hope, like theirs,
rests not on our performance but on God's faithful promise.

When your own faithfulness fails, remember this: God remembers His
covenant. That is a far surer foundation than anything in you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is my hope resting on my faithfulness or on God's promise?
2. How does it comfort me that God remembers His covenant even when I
   fail?
3. What does it mean to me to be counted among Abraham's heirs in Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that my hope rests on Your faithful promise, not on my
shaky performance. When I fail, remember Your covenant, sealed for me in
Christ. Amen.
